2 to the power of 10 is **1024**.

This is calculated as: 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 1024

Fun fact: this is why 1024 bytes is often called a "kilobyte" in computing, and it's the basis of the "kibibyte" (KiB) naming convention. Powers of 2 are fundamental to computing because computers work in binary (base 2).
